task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-165's implementation, commit 96292e1. Decision 0014 explicitly names SECURITY-REVIEWER as a hard gate 'on the whole WASM half' because plugins execute tenant-supplied input -- this is the FIRST WASM-half requirement, so this gate sets the pattern every future WASM requirement is judged against. This is also Letflow's FIRST native-code build dependency (a Rust NIF) -- a categorically different security surface than any prior Elixir-only or Lua-sandboxed code this project has shipped. Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md) and the real diff (git show 96292e1) in full before verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the process boundary (Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 under the existing, unmodified Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor) genuinely isolates a guest call the same way it does for existing in-process Elixir plugin handlers -- no new supervision gap introduced.

Confirm the moduledoc's residual-native-crash-risk disclosure (design section 7.2) is accurate and not understated -- specifically verify the claim that a NIF/Wasmtime crash is NOT observable/recoverable via Task.yield/2 or any supervisor, and that this is a real, accepted limitation of adopting any Rust-NIF-backed dependency, not specific to a bug in this implementation.
Confirm GenServer.stop/1 cleanup happens on EVERY path in run_trivial_guest/0 (success and error), so a failed/timed-out guest invocation cannot leak a live Wasmtime instance -- read the real code.

Confirm the trivial guest fixtures (priv/wasm_fixtures/*.wat) are genuinely trivial and harmless -- no capability, no I/O, no ambient access; this is not yet the full REQ-166 capability-gated ABI, so confirm this requirement doesn't accidentally grant more surface than its own stated trivial scope.

Confirm WASMEX_BUILD=true and the Rust toolchain pin do not introduce a supply-chain risk beyond what decision 0014 already accepted by choosing wasmex -- e.g. confirm the pinned Rust version (1.97.1) and wasmex version (~> 0.15.1) are pinned/ranged sanely, not unpinned to 'latest'.

Confirm no tenant-supplied data reaches the guest in this requirement's own trivial scope (the fixtures are checked-in, not tenant-controlled) -- this requirement does not yet handle real tenant WASM artifacts (that's REQ-166+), so confirm the design/implementation doesn't silently expand into that territory.

Cross-check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 explicitly, naming which apply (INV-3, sandboxing of untrusted code, is the most likely candidate given this touches the WASM half even in trivial form) and confirming each holds.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER gate on REQ-165 (commit 96292e1) -- PASS. Verified against the real diff, not the design doc's claims alone.
result.scope_test: APPLIES -- this diff adds Letflow's first native-code (Rust NIF) dependency and its first WASM guest-invocation code path, both named explicitly by decision 0014 and the handoff task as requiring this gate.

invariant_assessment.INV-1_tenant_data_isolation: NOT-APPLICABLE. No migration, no Ecto schema, no query against a tenant-scoped table. Confirmed via git diff --stat: only mix.exs, mix.lock, .tool-versions, ci.yml, letflow.check_toolchain.ex, plugin_handler.ex (new), two .wat fixtures (new), and the handler test are touched.
invariant_assessment.INV-2_server_side_field_auth: NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type or serialization boundary touched (S4 not started).
invariant_assessment.INV-3_untrusted_runtime_sandboxing: APPLIES (with a correction to blanket-defer). security-invariants.md gates this on 'S5's own build-vs-bind decision record' existing; docs/migration/decisions/0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md is Status: decided (2026-08-23), so the precondition is now met -- INV-3 is checkable, not automatically NOT-APPLICABLE, for any S5 diff going forward. HOLDS for this diff specifically: both req165_trivial.wat and req165_hang.wat declare zero imports -- no host function, no ambient network/filesystem access is bound to the guest at all in this requirement, so there is no capability surface to gate yet and the rule is satisfied vacuously (nothing reachable = nothing ungated). This requirement also does not yet grant any tenant-authored-script capability: fixtures are checked-in repo content, not tenant input, confirmed by reading priv/wasm_fixtures/*.wat and plugin_handler.ex's read_fixture/1 (reads from Application.app_dir(:letflow, 'priv'), a fixed relative path selectable only via node_config's 'wasm_fixture'/'export' keys -- no tenant-supplied bytes, no dynamic .wasm loading path exists anywhere in this diff). REQ-166 will need to design the actual host-capability allowlist before any host function is exposed; noting this explicitly so it isn't silently assumed already covered.
invariant_assessment.INV-4_secrets_by_reference: APPLIES (live). No secret material touched by this diff -- grep for System.get_env and the hardcoded-secret heuristic against lib/letflow/engine/wasm/ and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex both return zero hits. Rust/wasmex version pins (rust 1.97.1 in .tool-versions, wasmex ~> 0.15.1 in mix.exs, exact hex checksums for wasmex/rustler/rustler_precompiled locked in mix.lock) are version pins, not secrets -- out of INV-4's scope. HOLDS.
invariant_assessment.INV-5_not_found_forbidden: NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint (S4 not started).
invariant_assessment.INV-6_new_data_access_paths_prove_scopin: N/A as a distinct check -- this handoff itself is the proof INV-6 requires; satisfied by this document's explicit per-invariant assessment.
invariant_assessment.INV-7_no_sql_interpolation: APPLIES (live) but no hits. grep -rn 'Repo.query' lib/letflow/engine/wasm/ returns nothing -- this diff makes no Repo/SQL call at all. HOLDS.
invariant_assessment.INV-8_no_unhandled_crashes: APPLIES (live). Read plugin_handler.ex and the letflow.check_toolchain.ex diff in full: every external-I/O-touching call (File.read/1, Wasmex.start_link/1, Wasmex.call_function/4, System.cmd/2 for rustc) is wrapped in a case/with clause producing a tagged tuple, never a bare '{:ok, x} =' match on a call that can fail. running_rust_version/0 additionally wraps System.cmd/2 in rescue/catch specifically because it is the one new failure mode (missing rustc) this module's prior two comparisons structurally could not hit. grep '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' against plugin_handler.ex: zero hits. HOLDS.

acceptance_criteria_verification: AC1 (process boundary): CONFIRMED. plugin_interface.ex is byte-identical to main (git diff --stat main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex produces no output, also asserted by the shipped test). invoke/2,3 (read in full, lines 182-194) starts handle_node/1 inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 under the existing, unmodified Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor -- PluginHandler.handle_node/1 is dispatched through this exact path with no bypass, same as every existing in-process handler.

AC2 (residual native-crash-risk disclosure accuracy): CONFIRMED accurate, not understated. A Wasmtime/NIF segfault is a process-level (OS-process = BEAM-node) event; Task.yield/2 only observes the monitored Task's own exit signal, which a same-node hard crash never generates because there is no surviving process left to deliver it. No supervisor (Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor or any other) can restart what took the whole node down. This is a real, general, accepted limitation of adopting any Rust-NIF-backed dependency on the BEAM (a NIF crash is famously outside OTP's supervision model), not a defect specific to this implementation -- correctly scoped as such in the moduledoc (lines 41-56) and mirrored from plugin_interface.ex's own pre-existing 'Does NOT cover' disclosure.

AC3 (GenServer.stop/1 on every path): CONFIRMED by reading run_guest/2 (lines 104-111). The `with {:ok,bytes}<-read_fixture, {:ok,pid}<-start_instance do result=call_export(pid,export); GenServer.stop(pid); result end` shape means: (a) if read_fixture or start_instance fails, no Wasmex instance was ever started, so there is nothing to leak; (b) once an instance starts, GenServer.stop(pid) is an unconditional next statement after call_export/2 regardless of whether call_export returns {:ok,_} or {:error,_} (a trap) -- both the success and guest-trap paths clean up. The one path where the explicit stop is never reached is the AC5 hang path, where the outer Task is brutally killed before call_export returns; the design's own §5 residual note (and this diff's behavior) correctly relies on ordinary BEAM link semantics instead: Wasmex.start_link/1 is called from inside the Task process, so killing that Task with :brutal_kill also terminates its linked Wasmex GenServer via standard non-:normal-exit link propagation -- this is disclosed, not silently assumed, and is architecturally sound (not a leak).

AC4 (WAT fixtures trivial and harmless): CONFIRMED by reading both files verbatim. req165_trivial.wat: one exported func returning a constant i32, no imports, no memory, no other exports. req165_hang.wat: one exported func with an unconditional infinite loop, no imports, no memory. Neither module declares a single import -- there is no host function, no ambient capability of any kind reachable from either guest. Genuinely harmless.

AC5 (WASMEX_BUILD / toolchain pins not an unpinned supply-chain risk): CONFIRMED. rust 1.97.1 is an exact pin in .tool-versions (not a range), read into CI via a shell step + dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable's toolchain: input (no hardcoded second copy in ci.yml). wasmex is pinned to '~> 0.15.1' in mix.exs and locked to the exact version/checksum combination in mix.lock (wasmex 0.15.1, rustler 0.38.0, rustler_precompiled 0.9.0, each with a hex checksum). WASMEX_BUILD=true is scoped only to the 'Run backend gate' CI step (not the whole job), forcing a real cargo build rather than trusting a precompiled fetch -- this increases assurance (verifies the toolchain can actually build the native code) rather than introducing risk. No 'latest'/unpinned version anywhere in this diff.

AC6 (no tenant-supplied data reaches the guest; no silent REQ-166 expansion): CONFIRMED. read_fixture/1 resolves a path under Application.app_dir(:letflow, 'priv') -- always a path relative to the compiled release's own priv/ directory, never tenant-supplied bytes and never an absolute/traversal-controlled path from request input. The only caller-controllable inputs are node_config's 'wasm_fixture' and 'export' string keys, and in this diff's actual call sites (the handler's own tests) both are always one of the two checked-in fixture paths -- no dynamic loading of tenant .wasm/.wat content, no HTTP/upload path, no REQ-166 ABI (init/execute/deinit/get_capabilities/alloc) implemented. This requirement's scope is exactly what it claims: toolchain + process-boundary proof only.

AC7 (INV cross-check): see invariant_assessment above -- INV-1/2/5 NOT-APPLICABLE, INV-3/4/7/8 APPLY and HOLD, with INV-3's applicability corrected from a blanket 'deferred' to 'checkable now, satisfied vacuously' since decision 0014 (S5's build-vs-bind record) is already Status: decided.

AC8 (handoff status field): this file's top-level status is set to COMPLETED; mix letflow.lint_handoffs run with asdf shims on PATH reports 'OK -- 0 new violations across 1209 handoff files (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190)'.
result.verdict: PASS -- no BLOCKER found. This gate sets the pattern for the WASM half: future WASM requirements that expose actual host functions/capabilities to tenant-controlled guest code (REQ-166+) will need INV-3 re-verified against a real capability allowlist at that point, since this requirement's guest has zero imports and nothing to gate.
